items.title: Louis Hayes interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: got a quartet at the time with Frank Strozier and Harold Mabern

ctx.x: Was it a different experience to be making decisions, and what kind of decisions did you have to make as leader?

Well musically I was making decisions, and I felt very comfortable doing that. In that role I always felt comfortable with the guys and they felt comfortable with me, and I had this lady for management, see? So one of the problems I feel is — naturally working all the time is a major problem — but in that situation everybody really getting along — it seems like it’s very hard sometimes to get a group where everybody’s really compatible over a long period of time.
